name: Pushkar Breakfast Corner
why: The most-cited dawn food stall in Pushkar's main market square, a plastic-stool poha-and-chai setup among the morning fruit/veg hawkers. Runs 'every morning until the food finishes, usually before 10am' per the one source that mentions timing.
warn: No source confirms an actual opening time, only that it sells out before 10am. Do not assume this is open at 6-7am on arrival; treat it as a mid-morning bet, not a guaranteed dawn one.

name: Ugma ji ki Kachori Wale
why: The most-cited kachori stall in town, known for dal ki kachori with mango chutney.
warn: Timing reads as mid-morning across every source pulled; nothing confirms it running at 6-7am, so don't bank the dawn slot on it.

name: Kachori corner stall (behind Sri Raghunatha Swamy Temple)
why: An unnamed corner kachori-and-samosa stall about 2 minutes' walk from Market Square.
warn: Only the closing time (~5pm) is sourced; opening time is unknown, so don't count on this one before mid-morning either.

name: Lala Ji paratha stall
why: A stuffed-paratha stall on Main Market Road, explicitly an evening item.
warn: This is an after-5pm stall, not a dawn option — useful for a late-afternoon or evening snack, not the 6-8am window.

name: Main Market Square chai stall (unnamed)
why: A small combined grocery-and-chai stall in Main Market Square, described as 'available throughout the day.'
warn: No confirmed opening hour; the 'available throughout the day' phrasing implies but does not prove early availability.

name: Original Ganga Laffa and Falafel
priceNote: budget tier ($) on aggregator listings, no rupee figure sourced
why: Main-market falafel wrap stall, reviewers say 'one roll can feed two.' 4.8-star rating on one restaurant directory.
warn: Exact hours not sourced this session.

name: Shiva Laffa & Falafel Restaurant
priceNote: $$$ tier on aggregator, no rupee figure
why: Second named falafel stall in the main market, sister/rival to Ganga Laffa.
warn: Opening time (9am) is a single live aggregator snapshot taken ~2:20am IST on 6 Sept 2026 ('closed until 9AM'); closing time not found.

name: Government Bhang Shop, Pushkar
why: Rajasthan licenses specific 'Government Shop'-marked outlets to sell bhang (cannabis-leaf paste, legally distinct from banned parts of the plant) in Pushkar, Jaisalmer and Udaipur. Several unofficial rooftop cafes around Choti Basti also serve an unlabelled 'special lassi' understood locally to be bhang lassi.
warn: No source names the specific shop, its address, hours or price — this is a real, legal category of shop, not a single confirmed venue. Onset is slow and unpredictable (30 min-2 hrs), peak effect lands 2-4 hrs in, the whole experience can run 6-12 hrs, and dosing is inconsistent between vendors. If trying it: one small serving from a named government-marked shop (not an unmarked rooftop 'special lassi'), eaten with food already in the stomach, nothing else planned for the rest of the day.

name: Baba Ji Lassi Wale
why: One of the two most-cited named lassi shops in Pushkar travel writeups, near Brahma Temple.
warn: Could not fetch a live listing to confirm hours, price, or exact address this session — existence is well-attested by name across sources, nothing else here is independently verified.

name: Nataraj Lassi Wale
why: The second of the two most-cited named lassi shops in Pushkar, near Brahma Temple.
warn: Same gap as Baba Ji Lassi Wale — widely cited by name, hours/price/address unverified this session.

name: Kumawat Makhaniya Lassi
why: Cited by name for its makhaniya-style lassi (thick, topped with cream/rabri/gulkand, served in a clay cup) near Brahma Temple.
warn: A previously-seen ₹30 price figure for this stall traced back to an unsourced search summary, not a real citable page, so it is nulled here rather than repeated as fact.

name: Sunset Cafe (Hotel Sunset & Rooftop Restaurant)
priceNote: per person estimate; magicpin lists cost-for-two at ₹600
why: Famous rooftop over the lake near Sunset Point, trading heavily on its name and view. Woodfire pizza and Rajasthani thali are the draws.
warn: Closing time is genuinely inconsistent across aggregators (6am-11pm to 8am-midnight depending on source). One Tripadvisor reviewer reported an iron nail embedded in a pizza crust; other recurring complaints are indifferent staff, a dirty toilet, and prices 'quite a bit higher than average in town' for the name/location.

name: Honey & Spice
why: Healthy/organic breakfast cafe near Rangji Temple — smoothie bowls, gluten-free bakes, all dishes can be made vegan. One of the most consistently praised spots in town (4.6-4.8 across hundreds of reviews).
warn: Closes by 6pm, so it is not a dinner option. Cash-only payment is a real friction point for tourists.

name: Out of the Blue
priceNote: per person estimate from price-for-two ₹750; special thali ₹250
why: Four-floor rooftop on Main Market Road with a genuinely fantastic lake view; Israeli/Mexican/Indian fusion menu, owner Sandy praised by name repeatedly.
warn: Service is repeatedly called 'very slow.' A February 2026 review described the pasta as 'a nauseating experience' — recent quality is inconsistent despite the strong overall rating.

name: Funky Monkey Cafe
priceNote: per dish; Thai curries ₹180-220, ramen ₹200, sabich ₹140
why: Tiny espresso-and-fusion cafe near Mahadev Chowk — Thai/Japanese/Israeli/Italian small menu, genuinely good coffee, reliable WiFi.
warn: Very limited seating given the tiny space. One reviewer calls it 'the only place that serves eggs in Pushkar' — unverified as actual house policy, don't assume it. A separate review reports an inconsistent pet policy.

name: The Laughing Buddha Vegan Cafe
priceNote: sources disagree: ~₹100 per Wikivoyage, ₹200-400/person per Tripadvisor
why: Vegan/vegetarian fusion cafe on Main Market Road near Gau Ghat — banana bread with peanut butter, rose lassi, French-press Kerala coffee. Owner Sheru donates a share of profit to children's education.
warn: No strong complaint found; seating is small and the kitchen deliberately doesn't rush food, which reads as slow to some.

name: Cafe Lake View
why: The one named sit-down cafe with a sourced opening time before 9am — iced espresso, Nutella pancakes, peanut butter toast, right on Badri Ghat.
warn: Service is repeatedly called 'hit-and-miss.'

name: Om Shiva Garden Restaurant
priceNote: mains ₹70-170, buffet ~₹80 (Wikivoyage); price-for-two elsewhere cited as ₹550-750
why: Large shaded garden restaurant on the lake's eastern shore — wood-fired pizza, pasta, Indian thali, bakery/cake counter. No separate 'Shiva Garden' venue exists; it's the same place.
warn: Opening hour conflicts across sources: Tripadvisor's own Hours field says 7am, other aggregators say 9am — confirm on arrival before betting a dawn visit on this. Real complaints of raw garlic and an off smell in pasta, and one 1-star review calls it a 'cheat restaurant.' A separate review title claims it serves beer — unverified single-reviewer claim.

name: Third Eye Restaurant
priceNote: one source lists mains from ₹650/plate; a separate aggregator tags it as budget-tier ($) — genuinely conflicting, both reported
why: Mediterranean/Israeli restaurant running since 1996 on Jamni Kund Road — hummus, pita, falafel, smoothies.
warn: Waits up to two hours reported at peak evening hours; smoking is permitted on premises; most recent review surfaced is from Jan 2023, a real gap in fresh confirmation.

name: La Pizzeria
priceNote: pizzas from ₹180; per-person estimate ₹400-600 per aggregator
why: Wood-fired pizza in a candlelit pink-sandstone garden courtyard at Varah Ghat — spinach ravioli particularly praised.
warn: Higher priced than the town average and gets crowded by 7pm on weekends; one review reports a rude/arrogant owner and underwhelming vegetable portions despite the menu description.

name: Nirvana Cafe and Pizzeria
priceNote: moderate ($$-$$$) tier, no exact rupee figure sourced
why: 360-degree rooftop at Varah Ghat, called by one reviewer 'the best view of Pushkar, the lake and surroundings' — pizza, veg momos, falafel.
warn: The attached hotel side has serious cleanliness complaints ('filthy' rooms, stained sheets) and reports of rude staff and refund disputes — the restaurant's food reviews are more mixed than glowing, treat the two separately.

name: Cafe Nature's Blessing
why: Health-focused vegan/vegetarian cafe on Panch Kund Road — blueberry yogurt with seeds/nuts/honey, fenugreek toast with avocado and feta; half the menu is vegan per Wikivoyage.
warn: STATUS CONTESTED. HappyCow's listing shows it reported CLOSED in December 2022 (last dated review Feb 2020). Against that, an Instagram account under this name posted as recently as April 2026, and a food guide updated July 2026 still recommends it. Neither claim was independently confirmed with a live phone/Maps check this session — do not route a meal here without confirming on arrival.

name: A Cafe Enigma ("Enigma Garden")
why: Was a healthy-food/North-Indian cafe with a shady terrace; the rooftop was a juice/hangout spot only, never a food-serving rooftop, when it operated (was open 7:30am-11:30pm).
warn: CLOSED / DEFUNCT. Magicpin's own listing states the outlet has shut down. Do not route here.

name: Un-Earth Cafe
why: A coffee-and-books cafe with vegetarian/Rajasthani food.
warn: TEMPORARILY CLOSED per a current cafe guide. Do not route here without checking current status on arrival.

name: The Sixth Sense (Inn Seventh Heaven)
priceNote: sources range wildly from ₹200 to ₹2,400/person across aggregators; using the hiistories mid-range estimate
why: Rooftop restaurant atop the Inn Seventh Heaven haveli hotel — organic vegan/veg food, Buddha bowls, Rajasthani thali, smoothies, swing chairs, uses purified water to wash produce.
warn: One aggregator flags this listing as 'may be permanently closed,' and hours conflict sharply across sources — some say a continuous 8am-9pm, others a split shift with a 2pm-6pm midday closure, another says evening-only 6pm-9:30pm. Call ahead or verify before making this a meal anchor.

name: Rainbow Cafe (Choti Basti)
why: Simple home-style menu near Gautam Ashram — tawa roti, aloo soyabean, suji halwa. Distinct venue from the similarly-named Rainbow Restaurant on Brahma Mandir Road.
warn: Only one review visible on the source used — too little data for a reliable complaint pattern.

name: Rainbow Restaurant (Brahma Mandir Road)
why: Rooftop wood-fired pizza restaurant on Brahma Mandir Road — a separate business from Rainbow Cafe in Choti Basti despite sharing a name.
warn: Repeated hygiene complaints in reviews — staff reportedly seen spitting on the rooftop while diners ate, a rat sighting, and reviewers say 'prices have increased and quality has decreased.' Hours not sourced.

name: Pink Floyd Cafe
priceNote: veggie burger price only (₹90); overall tier is moderate ($$-$$$) per Tripadvisor, no fuller figure sourced
why: Psychedelic-rock-themed cafe and small hotel near Gautam Ashram in Choti Basti — one reviewer called its veggie burger 'the best veggie burger in India.'
warn: Recurring complaints of bad food execution, rude/slow staff, 'stale' food, and even ants found in tea. The listing itself is shown as unclaimed by management, and hours could not be sourced anywhere.

name: Honey Dew Cafe & Restaurant
why: Main Market Road/Badi Basti cafe — banana pancakes, strong coffee with honey, lentil pie. The owner cooks each dish to order.
warn: Three sources give slightly different hour ranges (7-9pm to 7:30-9:30pm); reviewers note service is slow precisely because food is made fresh per order.

name: Little Italy Pizzeria
why: Wood-fired pizza and white-sauce pasta on Panch Kund Road — one of the few sourced places running to 11pm, a genuine late-night candidate.
warn: A Wanderlog reviewer reported arriving to find it closed despite the posted hours — don't treat the '11pm' figure as guaranteed; call ahead for a late visit. One reviewer's dish also never arrived after the waiter got distracted upselling dessert.

name: Baba Restaurant (Om Baba Restaurant)
why: Popular Choti Basti rooftop (2nd floor, pool table below, overlooking a busy square) — chocolate banana porridge, veggie burgers, Oreo shake, 'Hello to the Queen' dessert. 4.5/5 over 562 reviews.
warn: Hours and price could not be sourced this session — Tripadvisor's own page would not load past a redirect. One travel-blog tip to 'bring insect repellent' is unconfirmed as a real recurring complaint.

name: Coffee Temple
why: Lake-view coffee spot at Varah Ghat — 'proper coffee' and oat cappuccino praised by reviewers.
warn: One travel blog calls its prices 'pretty steep' compared to nearby competitors.

name: R.S. Restaurant and Hotel
why: General Indian vegetarian restaurant/hotel near Brahma Temple, Badi Basti. One food-guide blog specifically credits it with fresh-made dal baati churma and an informal 'money-back if you don't like the first bite' guarantee, echoed by one reviewer.
warn: Hours are genuinely conflicting: one aggregator (restaurant-guru) gives 8am-10pm, but Tripadvisor's own Hours field literally says 'No hours available.' Reviews are also split hard — one calls it 'best Indian food in Pushkar,' another reports 'pathetic food quality' with staff turning abusive when the customer complained. Treat the money-back claim as an informal in-person practice, not a posted policy.

name: Shree Karni Maa Restaurant
priceNote: thali, unlimited refill except yogurt — per the (possibly stale) blog description below
why: Dal baati churma thali restaurant near Brahma Temple, Badi Basti, specifically cited by several undated travel blogs for its ₹200 all-you-can-eat-refill thali.
warn: STATUS CONFLICT — likely DEFUNCT. Zomato's own listing for this restaurant currently shows 'Permanently Closed' with zero dining ratings, directly contradicting the travel-blog praise (none of which carry a visible publish date to weigh against the Zomato status). Do not route a meal here without confirming on arrival; treat the ₹200-thali claim as describing a restaurant that may no longer be trading.

name: The Thali Garden Restaurant
priceNote: per person estimate from cost-for-two ₹500; a specific 'Elephant Special Thali' is priced separately at ₹299
why: Garden-set Rajasthani thali restaurant near Holi Ka Chowk, opposite Nagar Palika, Badi Basti — Elephant Thali, Backpacker's Thali, and Premium Thali variants. Confirmed as an active Zomato listing, 4.3/5 from 34 dining ratings.
warn: Closing time not found (only the 10:30am opening is confirmed) — small review sample (34 ratings) so treat the clean rating with some caution.

name: Jodhpuri Daal Bati Churma Restaurant
priceNote: one aggregator flags a $$$$ (expensive) tier, which conflicts with its own 'small dhaba-style place, average ambiance' description — unresolved, no rupee figure used
why: A dedicated dal bati churma specialist at Kundala Chauraha, Savitri (Mata) Road, Ganahera, near the railway crossing — further from the lake/bazaar core than the other thali spots, but consistently called authentic and tasty across sources (4.4/5, 148-220 reviews, count itself inconsistent across fetches).
warn: Only the closing time (10pm) is sourced; opening time not found. Described in one source as 'a small dhaba-style place with average ambiance' despite the high price tier shown elsewhere — a real, unresolved inconsistency.

name: Radhe Ji Restaurant (Varah Ghat)
why: Multi-cuisine restaurant opposite the Varah Ghat entry gate, Choti Basti, described by its own site as 'perfect for breakfast or any meal of the day.' Separate business from Radhey Ji Mishthan Bhandar, the sweet shop near Mahadev Chowk.
warn: No independent review platform (Zomato/Tripadvisor/Google) was located for this listing this session — the only material found is the business's own website and directory mirrors, so its praise is essentially self-reported and unverified. Hours and price not found.

name: Vaishnavi Bhojan Thali
why: Badi Basti North Indian thali restaurant, surfaced directly in a Pushkar thali/dal-baati search.
warn: Not independently reviewed elsewhere this session; hours unknown, and whether it specifically serves dal baati churma is unconfirmed.

name: Little Tibet Restaurant
priceNote: $$$ tier on aggregator, no rupee figure sourced
